title: Stability Orbit: Cross-Org Onboarding & Tactical Plan
content:
Overview:
This is a tactical activation plan for the "Stability Orbit" — a lightweight, repeatable cross-org onboarding and rollout pattern for SLOs and operational guardrails. The doc captures a 6-week cadence to get three pilot services to an agreed SLO baseline, validate alerts/runbooks, and hand off steady-state guardrails to service owners and SRE partners.

Context / motivation:
- We need a predictable, low-friction way to lift services into the company-wide dependability baseline without creating heavy policy blockers.
- Prior efforts were too prescriptive; this plan favors fast experiments + observable outcomes so teams can opt in and iterate.
- Output: validated SLOs, working runbooks, simple dashboards, and an escalation map that feeds into the platform ops oncall.

Goals (measurable):
1) Onboard 3 pilot services in 6 weeks to the baseline SLOs (availability 99.7% and p95 latency thresholds by category).
2) Reduce noisy pages from pilot services by 60% via improved alert thresholds + dedup rules.
3) Deliver a repeatable "onboarding kit" (template SLO, runbook, dashboard, triage play) and a short training session for feature teams.

Scope / out of scope:
- In scope: infra + platform dependencies (API gateway, inference pool autoscaler), 3 pilot services (one hosted-api, one dedicated, one private deployment demo), alert tuning, runbooks, dashboards, basic SLO telemetry.
- Out of scope: full enterprise SLA contract changes, deep model quality regressions (handled by product/optimize), wholesale refactors of service code.

Timeline (high level):
Week 0 (Prep): confirm pilots, align owners, baseline telemetry collection.
Week 1: Define service-specific SLOs and error budgets; draft runbooks.
Week 2: Implement dashboards and synthetic checks; establish alert routing to pilot channels.
Week 3: Run simulated degradations (chaos-lite) and incident play; tune alerts.
Week 4: Canaries + live traffic ramp; perform postmortems on any incidents.
Week 5: Finalize handoff artifacts, training session, and launch retro.
Week 6: Cutover to steady-state stewardship and backlog for scale.

Stakeholders / RACI (quick):
- Platform-engineering (Avery Kim): overall program lead, templates, infra work.
- Service owners (pilot teams): R for implementing SLOs, R for runbook completeness.
- Eng-SRE (Jordan Patel): C/A on incident handling playbooks and alert policies.
- Product-hosted-api (Maya Chen): C on acceptable latency bands and user impact mapping.
- Observability (Liam O'Rourke): R for dashboards + synthetic checks.
- Customer-success (inform): keep CS informed of planned experiments that might affect customers.

Tactical checklist (first pass):
- [ ] Confirm pilot contacts and get 2-week availability windows (Owner: Avery, due: 2026-02-16).
- [ ] Run baseline queries to capture 30 days of p50/p95/p99 and error-rate distributions (Owner: Observability, due: 2026-02-18).
- [ ] Draft per-service SLO doc and error budget policy (Owner: Service owner + Platform, due: 2026-02-21).
- [ ] Create dashboard template and import to pilot workspaces (Owner: Observability, due: 2026-02-24).
- [ ] Wire alert routing to pilot Slack channels and platform oncall (Owner: Eng-SRE, due: 2026-02-26).
- [ ] Run smoke/chaos tests and capture telemetry (Owner: Platform + Pilot, due: 2026-03-03).
- [ ] Triage noise and adjust thresholds (Owner: Eng-SRE, due: 2026-03-05).
- [ ] Handoff package assembled + training delivered (Owner: Platform, due: 2026-03-10).

Runbook / incident play quick template (to be copied into each service doc):
1) Observable signal definition (metric + threshold + window).
2) Knock-on customer impact mapping (who to notify).
3) Immediate mitigation options (restart, scale-up, route fallback).
4) Escalation path and paging rules (oncall -> SRE lead -> PL).
5) Post-incident notes + SLO impact calculations.

Success metrics / signals to watch:
- Time-to-detect (median and 90th) post-onboarding.
- Mean time to mitigate (for pages triggered during pilot).
- Page volume reduction (noisy duplicates suppressed).
- Percentage of SLO burn accounted for by platform vs. service-level issues.

Risk & mitigations:
- Risk: Pilot teams deprioritize tune work. Mitigation: schedule 2 dedicated pairing days and include a small shipped KPI tied to team roadmap.
- Risk: Alerts surface unrelated model-quality failures. Mitigation: add classification tags and run quick pre-filter rules; involve product/optimize to distinguish quality vs infra.
- Risk: Dashboarding/telemetry gaps in private deployment demo. Mitigation: use lightweight agent + synthetic probes; fallback to log-based indicators.

Communication plan:
- Weekly 30-min sync with stakeholders (Mon 10:00am).
- Slack channel: #stability-orbit (archived notes + action log).
- Biweekly update to eng leadership with a 1-slide summary and key blockers.

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Decide canonical SLO naming convention (service.shortname.api.availability vs feature-level). TODO: propose within 2 days.
- How tightly do we enforce error budget gating for releases during pilot? Leaning toward advisory mode for first run.
- Need templates for synthetic tests (obs team to share).

Next immediate steps (this week):
1) Ping pilot teams to lock pairing days (Avery).
2) Obs team to share dashboard JSON and a runbook example (Liam).
3) Schedule chaos-lite window and define fallbacks (Jordan + Platform).

Appendix: quick links and references:
- Minimal SLO templates: confluence://SLO-templates (draft)
- Incident playbook baseline: confluence://incident-playbook-compact
- Prior notes + experiments: GH issues tagged 'stability-orbit'

Notes on tone and expected artifact quality:
- This is intentionally a light, operational-first plan — goal is speed and learning. Iterate after pilots and capture what scales into a formal "onboarding kit".
- Keep runbooks concise and prescriptive; prefer bullet step actions vs long essays.

---
End of draft.

Feedback requested: please add any missing dependency (tools, infra credentials), push comments inline in this doc, and flag timeline conflicts for pilot teams.
